policy_title: Ensure independence for Britain's Armed Forces from EU programmes
stated: Reform UK will ensure the independence of Britain's Armed Forces from EU programmes, withdrawing from the EU Horizon programme, the European Defence Fund, and the EU’s military mobility project, to prevent them being 'sucked into an EU Command and Control Force'.

source.quote: Independence for Britain’s Armed Forces The government has signed up to the EU Horizon programme. That means we send money to the European Defence Fund and part of the EU’s military mobility project. Our Armed Forces are at risk of being sucked into an EU Command and Control Force.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly concerns national security and defence posture — withdrawing from EU defence programmes (European Defence Fund, military mobility project, and Horizon in its defence-research dimension) to preserve independent command-and-control of the Armed Forces is a substantive defence-posture decision that would earn a real verdict on safety and national security.

Withdrawal from EU Horizon (the world's largest research programme, to which the UK is now re-associated as a net recipient of collaborative research funding) would materially reduce UK access to research grants and cross-border innovation networks, with a non-negligible effect on the productivity and business-investment indicators.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: the sovereignty-vs-collective-security tradeoff on O5, and the concrete loss of Horizon research-funding access on O13. The European Defence Fund and military mobility project primarily bear on defence posture (O5) rather than generating separate fiscal (O12) or liberty (O10) effects large enough to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
